title: Food Spoilage — Milk, Meat, Poultry and Fish
shortDescription: What spoils animal foods, which organisms are responsible and how to recognise each pattern.
genZNote: High protein, high water, neutral pH — animal foods are basically a microbial all-you-can-eat. Learn each food's usual suspect.

sections.heading: Milk and Milk Products
bullets: Souring by lactic acid bacteria (Lactococcus lactis) ferments lactose; gas by coliforms; proteolysis and bitterness by psychrotrophic Pseudomonas/Bacillus enzymes that survive heat; ropiness by Alcaligenes viscolactis; sweet curdling by Bacillus.
Moulds spoil butter and cheese surface; yeasts in sweetened condensed milk and cream.
Control: cold chain, pasteurization, hygiene, UHT/aseptic.

sections.heading: Meat, Poultry and Fish
bullets: Meat: Pseudomonas (slime, off-odours aerobically), Lactobacillus/Brochothrix in vacuum packs (souring, greening), moulds on dried/cured meat; proteolysis and rancidity produce off-flavours.
Poultry: Pseudomonas, Salmonella, Campylobacter risk; spoilage visible as slime at ~10^7–10^8 CFU/cm².

Fish: high water, neutral pH, delicate flesh; TMAO reduced to trimethylamine (TMA, "fishy odour") by Shewanella and Pseudomonas; histamine formation in scombroid fish; rapid rigor/ autolysis; TVB-N and K value are freshness indices.
Control: chilling at 0 °C with ice, freezing at ≤ −18 °C, vacuum/MAP, salting/smoking, curing, canning.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Animal foods spoil rapidly because of their high moisture, nutrients and near-neutral pH; spoilage patterns depend on food type, storage temperature and packaging.

highYieldFacts: Pasteurization does not stop later psychrotroph enzyme spoilage if raw milk was poor.
commonTraps: Do not say all spoilage microbes are pathogens.
